_meta.review_notes: Writ of mandamus under Art 226 (HC) / Art 32 (SC). Strict pre-conditions: existence of public statutory duty, clear legal right in petitioner, demand and refusal, no equally efficacious alternative remedy (subject to exceptions). Mansukhlal Vithaldas Chauhan v. State of Gujarat (1997) 7 SCC 622 is leading authority. Will not issue against private parties, discretionary functions, or to direct legislation.

title: Writ Petition for Mandamus (Art. 226/32)

respondent_authority.label: Respondent Public Authority/Officer
respondent_authority.help: Designation, e.g., Secretary, Department of X, Govt. of Y

statutory_duty.label: Statutory Duty Sought to be Enforced
statutory_duty.help: Cite exact provision of statute imposing the duty

refusal_or_inaction.label: Refusal or Continued Inaction by Authority

mandatory_clauses: Identification of public authority and statutory duty
Prayer for issuance of writ of mandamus
Annexures including representation, refusal communication (if any)

prompt_context.tone: Constitutional writ — formal, precise on statutory duty, demand-and-refusal narrative.
must_cite: Article 226 (HC) or Article 32 (SC) of the Constitution of India
Specific section of statute imposing public duty on respondent
Mansukhlal Vithaldas Chauhan v. State of Gujarat (1997) 7 SCC 622 — conditions for mandamus
must_avoid: Seeking mandamus against private body without public function element
Seeking to control discretionary power (only legal discretion is reviewable)
Failing to plead demand and refusal

filing_checklist: Court fee as per HC/SC rules
Memo of parties with full addresses of public authority
Annexure: refusal or proof of inaction
Index + paging as per court rules

validation_rules.rule: MUST identify specific statutory provision imposing duty
MUST cite Mansukhlal Vithaldas Chauhan or equivalent
